title: Shape the partition, then place its replicas
description: Compare three keys for the same telemetry workload. The fixed sample exposes hot-partition risk, modeled partition size, token spread, and rack-aware replica placement without pretending to benchmark a real cluster.

keyShapes.label: Tenant only
keyShapes.detail: One long-lived partition receives every device event for a tenant.
keyShapes.consequence: A large tenant becomes one hot routing and storage unit. Replication creates copies of that hot partition; it does not split the write stream inside the partition.

keyShapes.label: Tenant plus day
keyShapes.detail: A daily bucket bounds retention, but every device in one tenant still shares the active bucket.
keyShapes.consequence: Time bucketing bounds partition growth and expiration work, but it does not remove a hot tenant. Add a stable distribution dimension when the query can name it.

keyShapes.label: Tenant, device, and day
keyShapes.detail: The query names a device and day, spreading current writes across device partitions.
keyShapes.consequence: The key matches a bounded device-by-day read and distributes concurrent writes. The application must fan out intentionally when it needs a tenant-wide query.
